newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Uganda plans coffee exports cut by 220,000 bags.
newsitem.headline: Uganda plans coffee exports cut by 220,000 bags.

text.p: Uganda's 1996/97 robusta coffee exports will be cut by over 200,000 60-kilo bags following talks among African producers this week on implementing a January world producers agreement, a Ugandan coffee official said on Friday.

"Our (production) forecast for 1996/97 is around 4.3 million bags but after the (robusta) cuts that will be about 4.08 million bags," Uganda Coffee Development Authority Secretary General William Naggaga told Reuters.

Naggaga was speaking on the sidelines of an InterAfrican Coffee Organisation meeting in Ivory Coast aimed at implementing a January-June robusta export limit of 850,000 bags for African producers agreed in January.
"Uganda's production is about 90 percent robusta and 10 percent arabica," said Naggaga. "The coffee will be held privately and will not be kept by the government," he added.
Nagagga said export limit quotas for each of Africa's major producers would not be set.
"It is a global export agreement," he said. "We will monitor export figures to achieve the aim."
IACO ends two days of talks on Friday on implementing the 850,000 bags cut agreed after an Association of Coffee Producing Countries meeting in Brazil in January.
Asked whether there was a need for export cuts after a recent explosion of the world price for robusta Nagagga said robusta prices still lagged behind arabica coffee prices.
"Robusta prices have improved substantially since the ACPC meeting but the differential between arabica prices and robusta is still there."
Naggaga said a rise in Uganda's output had resulted from wider cultivation and better farming practices.
Smuggled imports from neighbouring war-torn countries such as Zaire had been negligible, he added.
